c: Finely chop or mince the cooked chicken.
Sweat the onion in the butter without colour.
Add the chicken and heat through.
Add the flour and cook 1–2 min.
Add the hot milk gradually, whisking constantly; cook until very thick and the mix leaves the sides of the pan (core above 75 °C).
Stir in the Parmesan, mustard, parsley, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Spread on a tray, cover with film on the surface and blast-chill to below 5 °C within 90 min.
Portion the chilled mix at 35 g and shape into croquettes.
Bread: flour, then beaten egg, then panko.
Deep-fry at 170–175 °C for 3–4 min until golden; core temperature 75 °C.
Drain on a rack and serve 4 pieces per portion immediately.
72f3efc8.st: Croquette mix: 0–4 °C, 48 h. Breaded raw croquettes: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 1 month (fry from frozen at 165 °C to 75 °C core). Fried: serve immediately.
72f3efc8.al: 1 Gluten (wheat) · 3 Eggs · 7 Milk · 10 Mustard · 14 Sulphites (Dijon – check label)

c: Sauté the mushrooms in half the oil until all moisture has evaporated.
Sweat the onion in the remaining oil until soft and golden; add the garlic for the last minute. Chill to 0–4 °C.
Process the chickpeas to a coarse paste, keeping some texture.
Combine with the mushrooms, onion, rice, oats, cheese, mustard, soy sauce, parsley and spices; mix thoroughly.
Portion at 120 g and form patties 15–18 mm thick; chill 15–20 min.
Mix the panko, grated cheese and paprika.
Bread the patties: flour, then beaten egg, then the panko mix.
Deep-fry at 175 °C for 3–4 min until golden; core temperature 75 °C (finish at 180 °C convection for 3–4 min if needed).
Drain on a rack and use immediately.
aa33d0b5.st: Patty mix: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Breaded raw patties: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 1 month (fry from frozen at 165 °C, then oven to 75 °C core). Fried: serve immediately, do not hold.
aa33d0b5.al: 1 Gluten (wheat, oats, soy sauce) · 3 Eggs · 6 Soybeans · 7 Milk · 10 Mustard · 14 Sulphites (Dijon – check label)

c: Mix flour, starch, salt and pepper; whisk in the cold sparkling water to a thick pancake-batter consistency. Keep cold.
Peel the membrane; remove innards and quill. Cut into 1 cm rings and dry well.
Dip the rings in the batter.
Fry at 175 °C in small batches 1–2 min until golden; core 63 °C.
Drain on paper; serve at once with lemon wedges.
d0826bfa.st: Raw cleaned squid: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Fried: serve at once, do not hold.

c: Heat the water to 90–95 °C; add the vinegar.
Crack each egg into a separate cup; slide gently into the water.
Transfer at once to iced water; chill 1–2 min and trim excess white.
Hold chilled in cold water at 0–4 °C.
Preheat the combi oven to 64 °C, 100% steam.
Lay whole eggs in their shells in one layer in a perforated GN tray.
Chill in iced water; crack out carefully before service.
Reheat in water at 63–65 °C for 2–3 min until warmed through.
Drain and blot dry before plating.
Clean the mushrooms; cut into 2–4 cm pieces according to type.
Toss evenly with the oil and salt.
Spread in one layer in a perforated GN 1/1, with a solid GN 1/1 underneath to catch the liquid.
Combi oven, convection mode, 220 °C, 0% humidity, fan 100%: roast 15 min without stirring.
Stir; roast a further 5–10 min until lightly golden and dry.
Spread thinly and chill to below 5 °C within 90 min if not served at once.
Regenerate in a hot pan or combi oven to ≥ 75 °C. Serve 80 g per portion.
Rinse the rice in cold running water until the water runs clear.
Spread in a GN 1/1; add the water, salt and butter.
Cover tightly with a lid or foil. Cook at 100 °C, 100 % steam, for 25–30 min.
Rest covered 5–10 min; fluff with a fork. Serve 150 g.
29200be5.st: Hold at ≥ 63 °C, max 2 h. For later use blast-chill to \< 5 °C within 90 min; 0–4 °C, 24 h; reheat once to ≥ 75 °C.

c: Chill the cream to 2–4 °C; whip to soft peaks.
Mix the cream cheese, icing sugar and vanilla until smooth.
Fold the whipped cream into the cheese mixture.
Chill at 0–4 °C for 20–30 min before use.
Use 45 g per waffle (Belgian or bubble waffles, pancakes).
Pick the basil leaves, discard the stems; wash with the spinach.
Blanch in the boiling salted water for 10 s; refresh in iced water for 1 min.
Squeeze completely dry in a cloth and chop roughly. Chill the oil to 4 °C.
Blend the leaves and oil at maximum speed for 6–7 min until 65–70 °C (Thermomix: 70 °C, speed 10, 7 min). Do not exceed 70 °C.
Cool immediately in a bowl over ice, stirring, to set the colour.
Hang in muslin or a coffee filter at 0–4 °C for 3 h to overnight. Do not press.
Decant into squeeze bottles; label and date.
Process the shallot, garlic, anchovies and capers to a smooth paste.
Wash, dry and finely chop the parsley, chives and tarragon.
Whip the butter until light and pale.
Add the paste, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, brandy, lemon juice, paprika, curry powder, white pepper and salt; mix well.
Fold in the herbs until completely homogeneous.
Roll into a 4 cm cylinder in cling film or pipe into silicone moulds (10 g); chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Label and date.
8f22c036.al: 4 Fish (anchovy) · 7 Milk · 10 Mustard · 14 Sulphites (Dijon, Worcestershire, capers – check label) · Worcestershire sauce, curry powder: check label

c: Dice the butter evenly; place in a heavy-based pan.
Let the water boil off and the foam rise.
Continue heating until the milk solids settle and brown.
At 150–160 °C, when amber with a hazelnut aroma, remove from heat at once.
Strain through muslin or a fine filter.
Chill to ≤ 4 °C in a closed container.
Beat the soft butter with the crumbled blue cheese until smooth.
Roll into logs in film; chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Portion 20 g for beef and roasted vegetables.
Beat the soft butter with shallot, mustard, anchovy paste and capers.
Add parsley, tarragon, lemon juice, salt and pepper; mix until even.
Roll into logs in film; chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Portion 20 g for steaks and grills.
ffdb7803.al: 4 Fish (anchovy) · 7 Milk · 10 Mustard · check label (mustard, anchovy paste)

c: Combine the chili flakes and paprika with the cold oil in a small heavy saucepan.
Heat to 70 °C and hold 30 min, stirring occasionally. Do not let it fry.
Remove from the heat, cover and infuse 2 h at room temperature.
Settle, then decant the clear top layer.
Mix all in a heatproof stainless-steel container.
Put the oil and aromatics in a saucepan; heat gradually to 110–120 °C.
Hold at that temperature until the aromatics are lightly golden, ≈20 min. Do not let it smoke.
Strain through a fine chinois; discard the aromatics.
Reheat to 125 °C; pour one third over the chilli base, stirring.
Reheat the rest to 145 °C; pour the second third, stirring.
Heat the final third to 170 °C (never above 180 °C); pour carefully, stirring.
Cool, transfer to sterilised containers and mature 12–24 h at 0–4 °C.
568f32cb.st: 0–4 °C, 30 days, sealed. Do not store at ambient.

c: Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Soften the butter at room temperature (max. 1 h).
Beat in garlic, parsley, lemon juice and salt until even.
Roll into logs in film; chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Portion 20 g slices for steaks, vegetables or bread.
Grate the garlic to a smooth paste.
Whip the butter until light and pale.
Add the garlic, parsley, lemon juice, salt and white pepper; mix until completely homogeneous.
Roll into a 4 cm cylinder in cling film or pipe into silicone moulds (10 g).
Chill at 0–4 °C until firm; label and date.
Use garlic confit that has been kept at 0–4 °C (garlic in oil: botulism risk at ambient).
Beat in the soft butter, salt, pepper, lemon juice and chopped herbs.
Roll in film into a log; chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Portion 20 g slices.
Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Pick and wash the parsley and spinach.
Blanch 10–15 s in boiling salted water.
Blend with the oil 2–4 min until it warms to 60–65 °C.
Strain through a sieve lined with muslin, without pressing.
Chill to ≤ 4 °C in a closed container.
Wash, dry thoroughly and finely chop all herbs.
Whip the butter until light and pale.
Add the herbs, lemon zest, lemon juice, salt and white pepper; mix until evenly combined.
Roll into a 4 cm cylinder in cling film or pipe into silicone moulds (10 g).
Chill at 0–4 °C until firm; label and date.
Wash the leek tops, split lengthways and dry thoroughly.
Spread on a tray and char at 250 °C convection (full extraction) for 40–60 min until completely black and brittle; any green left tastes bitter and raw.
Cool, grind to a fine powder and pass through a fine sieve.
Blend the leek ash with the oil at high speed for 2 min.
Rest 1 h, then pass through a fine chinois lined with one layer of muslin; fine ash must stay in suspension for the black colour.
Bottle; label and date. Shake before use.
60347866.st: 0–4 °C, 3 weeks; −18 °C, 3 months. Leek ash: airtight, dry, ambient, 1 month.

c: Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Beat the soft butter with lemon zest, juice, dill and salt until even.
Roll into logs in film; chill at 0–4 °C until firm. Portion 20 g for fish, seafood and vegetables.
Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Pick the parsley leaves, discard the stems; wash with the spinach.
Blanch in the boiling salted water for 10 s; refresh in iced water for 1 min.
Squeeze completely dry in a cloth and chop roughly. Chill the oil to 4 °C.
Blend the leaves and oil at maximum speed for 6–7 min until 65–70 °C (Thermomix: 70 °C, speed 10, 7 min). Do not exceed 70 °C.
Cool immediately in a bowl over ice, stirring, to set the colour.
Hang in muslin or a coffee filter at 0–4 °C for 3 h to overnight. Do not press.
Decant into squeeze bottles; label and date.
Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Temper the butter to 16–18 °C. All additions must have a dry surface.
Roll into 3–4 cm logs; vacuum-pack and chill to 0–2 °C.
Dose 15–20 g per portion of meat after cooking and resting.
Cut 5–10 mm off the top of the garlic heads to expose the cloves.
Brush with the olive oil and wrap tightly in foil.
Roast at 170 °C convection for 35–45 min until the cloves are soft and golden.
Cool, squeeze the cloves from the skins and pass to a smooth purée. Chill to 0–4 °C before use.
Soften the butter to 18–20 °C and whip until light and pale.
Add the roasted garlic purée, smoked paprika, parsley, lemon juice, salt and white pepper.
Roll into a 4 cm cylinder in cling film or pipe into silicone moulds (10 g).
Chill at 0–4 °C until firm; label and date.
57ddb673.st: 0–4 °C, 7 days; −18 °C, 3 months. Roasted garlic purée: 0–4 °C, 72 h.

c: Whisk the paprika into the cold oil in a small heavy saucepan.
Heat gently to 60–65 °C and hold 30 min, stirring occasionally. Above 70 °C the paprika scorches and turns bitter.
Remove from the heat and settle at room temperature for 2–3 h.
Decant the clear top layer without disturbing the sediment.
Beat the soft butter with icing sugar, honey and vanilla until light and fluffy.
Pipe or roll into logs; chill at 0–4 °C. Portion 20 g for pancakes, waffles and toast.
Whisk the turmeric and coriander into the cold oil in a small heavy saucepan.
Heat to 70 °C and hold 20 min, stirring occasionally.
Remove from the heat and settle at room temperature for 2–3 h.
Decant the clear top layer, then filter through a coffee filter.
Bottle; label and date. Turmeric stains boards and cloths: use dedicated equipment.

2f6e757d.yl: Yield: 2 baguettes · 10 portions × 3 slices · Portion: ≈ 70 g
c: Beat soft butter with crushed garlic, chopped parsley, Parmesan and salt.
Slice baguettes 2 cm on the bias, not quite through (or open lengthwise).
Spread 7 g garlic butter per slice; wrap in foil.
Bake 200 °C 10 min, open the foil, 4–5 min more until crisp; serve hot.
2f6e757d.st: Garlic butter 0–4 °C 7 days, freeze 1 month. Buttered bread: bake within 24 h.

f29d8e39.yl: Yield: 12 flatbreads × 80 g · Portion: 1 flatbread = 80 g
c: Mix all except butter 6 min to a soft dough; prove 1 h at 26 °C until doubled.
Divide 85 g; round; rest 10 min; roll Ø 20 cm, 4 mm thick.
Cook in a dry, very hot pan or griddle (250 °C) 60–90 s per side until puffed and charred in spots.
Brush with melted butter (optional herbs or za'atar); stack under a cloth.
f29d8e39.st: Room temp. 24 h wrapped; freeze −18 °C 1 month; reheat on the griddle 20 s per side.

c: Thaw frozen octopus at 0–4 °C for 24 h. Wash well; remove beak and any remains.
Bring the water to the boil; dip the tentacles 2–3 times for a few seconds so they curl.
Add onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf and pepper; submerge the octopus.
Simmer at 90–95 °C for 40–50 min until tender; add the salt for the last 10 min.
Cool in the broth no more than 30 min, then in an ice bath to below 4 °C within 90 min.
Trim sinew and excess fat; mince twice through a 4–6 mm plate. Keep the meat below 4 °C.
Add onion, egg, salt, pepper, garlic, cream and breadcrumbs; mix 2–3 min in a mixer until elastic.
Shape 165 g patties, 1.5–2 cm thick, using a ring.
Grill 3–4 min per side, or pan-fry in oil 3–4 min per side then finish covered on low heat 5 min (or 180 °C convection 6–8 min).
464aa720.st: Raw patties: 0–4 °C, 24 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Cooked: 0–4 °C, 72 h.

c: Use only mackerel frozen to a core of −20 °C for at least 24 h, or −35 °C for at least 15 h (parasite control); keep the supplier certificate on file. The cure and marinade below do not kill parasites.
Thaw at 0–4 °C. Remove the pin bones and pat the fillets dry.
Mix the salt, sugar, lemon zest, pepper and bay leaf.
Coat the fillets evenly and cure at 2–4 °C for 8–12 h.
Rinse lightly under cold water and dry thoroughly.
Bring all marinade ingredients to the boil; remove from the heat and cool to below 4 °C.
Lay the cured fillets in a non-reactive container and cover completely with the cold marinade.
Drain, slice and portion 90 g per portion with a few shallot rings.
41c21f35.st: In the marinade, 0–4 °C, 5 days. Label with production date. Not suitable for freezing after marinating.
41c21f35.al: 4 Fish (mackerel) · 14 Sulphites (white wine vinegar — check label)

c: Slice the chicken across the grain 3–4 mm thick.
Mix the remaining ingredients; coat the chicken evenly.
Add the chicken in batches, stirring gently, 30–60 s until white; lift out and drain.
This is par-cooking only: finish in the wok or sauce to core 75 °C, or chill to below 4 °C within 90 min.
fb633d86.st: Marinated raw: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Velveted: 0–4 °C, 48 h; −18 °C, 1 month.

c: Stir all together until the salt and sugar dissolve. Chill to 0–4 °C.
Submerge the breasts fully in the cold brine; refrigerate at 0–4 °C for 90–120 min.
Remove, pat dry; do not rinse.
Lay on a rack and refrigerate uncovered 2–12 h to dry the surface.
Sear in a very hot pan with the oil, 2–3 min per side until golden.
Finish in a convection oven at 160 °C to a core temperature of 75 °C.
Rest 5 min; slice. Portion at 200 g.
6258adbd.st: Raw brined: 0–4 °C, 24 h. Cooked: 0–4 °C, 72 h; −18 °C, 3 months. Reheat to 75 °C core.

c: Slice the onions into thin half-moons.
Sweat in the oil with the salt, 10–15 min, without colour.
Cook slowly over low heat 60–90 min, stirring often, to a deep caramel colour.
Add sugar and balsamic; reduce to a jam consistency.

dd8553c9.yl: Yield: 1 batch ≈ 160 g (16 × 10 g) · Portion: 10 g
c: Mix the beetroot juice with the balsamic vinegar and salt.
Whisk in the agar-agar and boil 1–2 min, stirring.
Pour into a tray and set at 0–4 °C, about 30 min.
Blend until smooth and glossy; transfer to a squeeze bottle.
dd8553c9.st: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Not suitable for freezing (agar gel weeps on thawing).

c: Wrap the beetroot in foil; roast in a convection oven at 180 °C for 60–90 min until completely tender.
Peel while warm (≈ 750 g flesh); cut into pieces.
Blend hot with the butter and cream until completely smooth.
Pass through a fine chinois or tamis.
Season; adjust consistency with a little cream if needed.
Cool to below 5 °C within 90 min if not served at once.
Serve 50 g per portion, hot (≥ 63 °C). Pairs with venison, duck, beef and goat's cheese.
Slice the onions into thin half-moons, 2–3 mm.
Heat butter and oil in a heavy-based pan.
Add onions and salt; cook over low heat, stirring often.
Caramelise 60–90 min to a deep amber colour, deglazing with small amounts of the water to prevent burning.
Add the sugar for the last 10 min.
Cook the carrots slowly in the butter at 90 °C (covered, oven convection 95 °C) for 60–80 min until fully soft and glossy.
Serve hot (≥ 63 °C) or blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min.
Cut the carrots into even 1–2 cm pieces; spread in GN 1/1, 40 mm deep, max. 3–4 cm layer. Season evenly with salt.
Combi oven: Combi mode 160 °C, 20% humidity, fan speed 2/5, vent 60%, 50–55 min until fully soft; stir once after 25 min.
Transfer immediately to the blender while hot (60–80 °C).
Blend, adding the cold butter gradually, to a smooth emulsion; adjust texture with hot water.
Hold for service at ≥ 63 °C, or blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min.

1f52f399.yl: Yield: ≈ 800 g tomatoes + 450 g oil · 20 portions · Portion: 40 g
c: Wash and dry the tomatoes completely; prick each once with a needle.
Lay in one layer in a shallow GN tray with the garlic, herbs, salt, sugar, pepper and zest.
Pour over the oil to cover 70–80% of the tomatoes.
Cook in a convection oven at 90–95 °C for 1.5–2.5 h until soft and lightly wrinkled but whole.
Cool in the oil to below 5 °C within 90 min; keep covered with the oil.
Serve 35 g tomatoes with 5 g of the oil per portion. Use the remaining aromatic oil for dressings and sauces within the same shelf life.
1f52f399.st: 0–4 °C, 4 days, fully covered with oil (garlic in oil — botulism control). Never hold at ambient. Do not freeze.

c: Blend all ingredients until fully emulsified; re-blend before each pour.
Heat a non-stick pan (Ø 20 cm) over medium heat to 170–180 °C surface; no extra fat.
Pour ≈12 g batter into a thin 1–1.5 mm layer.
Cook undisturbed until the water has boiled off and a lacy, porous structure forms, ≈2–3 min.
When fully dry and lightly coloured, lift with a spatula.
Drain and cool on absorbent paper until crisp.
e0ea7de4.st: Airtight container with silica gel, ambient, 24 h. Do not refrigerate.

d028433d.yl: Yield: 225 g (56 portions × 4 g) · Portion: 4 g
c: Batch · Yield 225 g · use 22 g per 1 kg fries
Weigh all ingredients and mix thoroughly; pass through a coarse sieve to break up lumps.
Store in an airtight labelled container.
Season fries within 30 s of leaving the fryer, while hot and still glossy: 22 g per 1 kg fries (4 g per 180 g portion). Toss to coat evenly.
d028433d.st: Airtight, dry and dark, ambient ≤ 20 °C: 3 months.
d028433d.al: None of the 14 listed allergens. Spices: check label.

c: Cover the garlic and thyme completely with oil.
Cook at 85–90 °C (oven, convection 90 °C) for 60–90 min until creamy.
Blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min; keep covered in oil.
b36ca3a2.st: 0–4 °C, 4 days; −18 °C, 3 months. Never store garlic in oil at room temperature (botulism risk).

c: Place the garlic in a deep tray; cover completely with oil.
Cook at 90–95 °C (oven, convection 95 °C) for 60–90 min, without boiling, until fully soft.
Lift out the garlic; blend with salt and about 200 g of the oil until smooth and emulsified.
Blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min; keep the strained oil chilled for other use.
89ba74f1.st: 0–4 °C, 4 days; −18 °C, 3 months. Garlic in oil: never store at room temperature (botulism risk).

c: Cover the garlic with 1 L cold water, bring to the boil, drain. Repeat 3 times.
Cover with the milk; cook at 90–95 °C for 20–30 min until fully soft.
Blend the garlic with cream, butter, salt and about 100 g of the milk until smooth.

016f6adc.yl: Yield: 1 batch ≈ 280 g (28 × 10 g) · Portion: 10 g
c: Boil the peas in salted water 3–4 min; drain and refresh in iced water.
Blend with the vegetable stock, olive oil and salt until smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Whisk in the agar-agar and boil 1–2 min, stirring.
Pour into a tray and set at 0–4 °C, about 30 min.
Blend again until smooth and glossy; transfer to a squeeze bottle.
016f6adc.st: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Not suitable for freezing (agar gel weeps on thawing).

c: Sweat the shallot in the butter without colour.
Add the hot stock; cook until the peas are just tender, 3–4 min.
Add the mint; blend immediately at high speed until smooth.
Pass through a fine chinois or tamis; season.
If not served at once, cool over ice to below 5 °C within 90 min to keep the colour.
Serve 50 g per portion, hot (≥ 63 °C). Pairs with lamb, white fish, scallops and asparagus.
48954c20.al: 7 Milk · vegetable stock: check label (9 Celery)

c: Mix the sugar and agar thoroughly.
Heat the water to 40–50 °C and whisk in the sugar-agar mix.
Bring to a full boil and simmer 1–2 min to hydrate the agar fully.
Remove from the heat and cool to 60–65 °C.
Stir in the lemon juice and zest.
Pour into a shallow tray and chill at 0–4 °C until completely set (≈ 1 h).
Blend until perfectly smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Transfer to squeeze bottles; label and date.
3f80d6eb.st: 0–4 °C, 3 days. Do not freeze (gel weeps on thawing).

c: Wash and dry the potatoes; do not peel. Prick lightly.
Place on a bed of coarse salt in a GN tray.
Bake, convection 185 °C, 70–90 min, to a core of 96–98 °C.
Cut open while hot; scoop out the flesh.
Pass through a ricer or tamis.
Beat in the cold butter until fully absorbed.
Add cream heated to 70–80 °C gradually until silky; season with salt.
Wash the seeds thoroughly to remove all melon flesh.
Soak in cold water at 0–4 °C for 4–8 h.
Drain and rinse well; discard the soaking water.
Blend the seeds with 700 g cold water and the salt at high speed for 2–3 min until smooth.
Chill immediately to 0–4 °C; bottle, label and date.
Blanch the orange slices in boiling water 2 min; drain. Repeat 3 times (1 L each).
Bring sugar and syrup water to the boil.
Add the oranges; cook at 90 °C for about 2 h until the peel is translucent and glossy.
Cool in the syrup; chill to ≤ 4 °C.
Rub the belly with salt and pepper; cure 12–24 h at 0–4 °C.
Pat dry; submerge in lard melted to 90 °C.
Cook in the oven, convection 90 °C, 3 h until collagen is fully broken down (core well above 75 °C).
Cool in the fat; press if needed and blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 90 min.
Portion 155 g; sear skin-side down until crisp, finish in the oven at 200 °C to a core of 75 °C.
6ee386c6.st: Covered in fat or vacuum-packed: 0–4 °C, 7 days; −18 °C, 3 months.

fe7baecf.yl: Yield: 1 batch ≈ 240 g (24 × 10 g) · Portion: 10 g
c: Roast the peeled, diced pumpkin at 180 °C convection 25–30 min until soft.
Blend with the orange juice, ginger and salt until smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Whisk in the agar-agar and boil 1–2 min, stirring.
Pour into a tray and set at 0–4 °C, about 30 min.
Blend again until smooth and glossy; transfer to a squeeze bottle.
fe7baecf.st: 0–4 °C, 72 h. Not suitable for freezing (agar gel weeps on thawing).

c: Wrap ≈ 400 g raw beetroot in foil; roast in a convection oven at 180 °C for 60–90 min until completely tender. Peel while warm; weigh 300 g.
Blend the beetroot with the water until smooth; pass through a fine sieve.
Whisk in the agar; bring to the boil and simmer 1 min, whisking.
Stir in the lemon juice, salt and sugar.
Pour into a shallow tray; chill at 0–4 °C until fully set.
Cut into cubes; blend until smooth and glossy (adjust with 10–20 g cold water if too thick).
Pass through a fine sieve; fill squeeze bottles.
b0d6e0ca.st: 0–4 °C, 5 days. Do not freeze (the gel weeps).

c: Use salmon frozen at −20 °C for at least 24 h (parasite control), thawed at 0–4 °C.
Portion 140 g; salt lightly 20 min before cooking.
Heat the oil with thyme to 52 °C (water bath or combi steam 52 °C).
Submerge the salmon; cook 25 min to a core of 50 °C.
Serve at once; for later use, blast chill to ≤ 4 °C within 60 min.
3e9fc6bc.st: 0–4 °C, 24 h, covered in oil. Not suitable for freezing.

c: Weigh all dry ingredients into a dry bowl.
Grind finely in a dry blender or spice grinder until even.
Store airtight. Use 10 g per 100 g of chips or potatoes; 20 g + 100 g sour cream for a dip.
cfb41fed.st: Airtight, dry and dark at 15–20 °C, 3 months.
cfb41fed.al: 7 Milk · check label (sour cream powder, butter powder)

c: Peel and halve the pears (1.5 kg whole); remove the core. Brush with lemon juice.
Vacuum-pack 2 halves per bag with honey, butter and spices.
Cook in a combi oven on steam at 85 °C (or water bath 85 °C) for 60–90 min until tender.
Serve warm, or chill in iced water to below 4 °C within 90 min.
Dice the cucumbers and onion to 2–3 mm (or pulse briefly in a food processor).
Toss with the salt; stand 30 min at 0–4 °C.
Drain and squeeze out the excess liquid.
In a saucepan combine the vinegar, sugar, 20 g of the water, mustard, mustard seeds, celery seeds and turmeric; bring to a gentle boil.
Slake the corn starch in the remaining 20 g cold water; whisk into the simmering liquid.
Add the cucumber and onion; simmer 3–5 min, stirring, until lightly thickened.
Cool rapidly to below 5 °C within 90 min.
fbb88cbe.al: 9 Celery (celery seed) · 10 Mustard · Dijon, vinegar: check label (14 Sulphites)

c: Cut the crustless bread into even 1–1.2 cm cubes.
Warm the clarified butter and olive oil with the garlic and thyme on low heat 5 min without colour; strain.
Toss the bread with the warm infused fat, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Spread in one layer on a lined tray; bake at 155–160 °C convection for 12–15 min, stirring once.
Bake until evenly golden and dry right through. Cool on the tray at room temperature.
Caesar salad: toss with finely grated parmesan at service.
Cream soups: add on top at service only.

Pack into clean sanitised jars with the dill; cover completely with the cold brine.
Close and keep at 0–4 °C. Pickle min./best: radish 6/12–18 h; cucumber, pepper 12/24 h; cauliflower 12/24–36 h; carrot 12/36 h.

Cover with the cold water in a stockpot; bring slowly to a simmer, skimming continuously.
Add the vegetables, garlic, bay, peppercorns and parsley stems.

Cool rapidly: from 60 °C to below 10 °C within 2 h (ice bath or blast chiller), then to 0–4 °C.
